analysis: Both changed files are docs only (docs/developer/test.md, docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md); no executable code or security controls are modified in the supplied evidence. test.md head lines 177-217 add an opt-in live test section (ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests). It uses an isolated ephemeral cache, `env -i` with a minimal environment and a non-production report output, and refuses MiMo specs. It does not use production cache roots or keys, and it does not weaken the existing 'never use production cache roots/keys' guidance at line 163. ssd-kv-cache.md adds a 'Provider-staged destinations' row (patch hunk @@ -116,6 +117, new line 119) describing a behavior change in the unseen source: provider-staged imports now build destinations from zeroed host bytes and skip eval/stream fences, so staging avoids MLX evalLock. It also notes the zero source may briefly commit up to one destination outside the MLX allocator, and the import plan charges that as staging scratch. Relevant threat context: T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache, TTFT oracle, SSD tier), TB-007 and T-028. The doc states per-condition donor/cache scope separation and tenant refusal checks. The code (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift) is not in this batch. So the following are unverified: that the zero-initialized host destination is fully overwritten with authenticated data before use, that the memory admission accounting is correct, and that restore timing does not widen the T-041 timing oracle. A later pass should review those source files if available. No finding is raised from documentation alone.
